questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Lot of exchange spots available here and my grades were not good enough to get into the more popular exchange places.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great city, not that great a university. The Erasmus team at the University is doing a pretty good job at creating opportunities to meet new people.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy if you are persistent. A lot of the information is in Italian, but you can find the information if you use Google translate and ask the administrative staff on campus.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Some assistance filling out my learning agreement and then some assistance from the professors in changing courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They could have had an official orientation, I did not find any info about that anywhere.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, I used spotahome. The site itself is good, but be careful of scammers and landlords trying to cheat you of your deposit.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's better, but more expensive. The Erasmus housing is cheaper, but you have to share a room with someone random and the building is very old. So I preferred finding something on my own.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not really relevant since I did not use the housing provided for students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A bit confusing, but could have been worse. Compared to UCPH, which is also kind of confusing the first time.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think I had to fill out a form online, but I honestly can't remember exactly how. But I received clear guidance via email, so it wasn't that hard to register for the university itself.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I received a thorough email describing how to do it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register to any course I would like to. It was easy and if I had any questions I could ask the professor on the course in question. I had to change a course, and that went smoothly.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the emails you receive and use Google translate and contact the administrative staff if you have any issues. The Erasmus office is pretty good at helping you, when it's confusing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The educational level is pretty low compared to UCPH and some of the professors are not fluent in English. So don't choose Milan for an academic challenge.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Much lower academic level compared to UCPH, much of the content was introductory and the course contents were confusing and incoherent at times. They focus on learning things by heart, which is not really a very effective way to actually learn something instead of learning the students to analyse and use the theories themselves.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty much the same, classroom teaching and some group projects. They check attendance sometimes, but not consistently and the academic level is lower.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Global Criminal Organizations, International Law, Multi-Level Legal Systems, Global Politics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International Law because the professor is able to speak English properly and actually try to teach the students to analyse and use the course literature on real cases. Global politics is also okay, but if you're studying political science at UCPH, you will probably have read all the course literature before. I recommend choosing some courses at first and then changing afterwards, once you have assessed if the professor is able to teach in English.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My landlord tried to keep my deposit and ending up taking some of it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing is more expensive than expected. Transportation however is very cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The Erasmus group are hosting a bunch of activities that you can join making it easy to find new friends.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Tuesday bars, pubcrawls, football and other sport activities arranged by the students themselves. And short day trips outside Milan.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to some parties and Erasmus activities to find new friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See other cities, the trains is cheap and it is easy to visit Rome, Florence, Turin, Venice, Bologna etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, Italy is still Europe so not that different from Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Nope, I did not really socialize with the Italian students, only international students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not really find anything that culturally challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food is amazing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be careful not to get scammed when finding an apartment, take advantage of the food and restaurant scene in Italy and go visit some other cities around Milan.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to go to some Erasmus events alone and make new friends, it pays off.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seeing Italy and enjoying the Italian cuisine.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding friends in the beginning, and the academic level at the university, which were disappointing to say the least.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Nope.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
